subject: Polyglot suitability readout + next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Muller <anna.muller@linguix.ai>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@globexpayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Polyglot suitability readout + next steps

Hi Anna / Rahul — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary from discovery:
- Primary production use: customer support routing + payment instruction extraction (sensitive spans).
- Monthly volume: ~120k queries; peak bursts during EMEA business hours.
- Priority languages: German (de), French (fr), Japanese (ja), Hindi (hi).
- Hard constraints: data residency for EU customers and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

High-level model recommendations (first-pass):
1) rw-multilang-7B-v2-quant (balanced latency/cost for multilingual NLU) — good for routing + short extraction.
2) rw-instruct-13B-multilingual (higher fidelity for structured extraction, use for critical payment instructions).
3) fallback: openlm-7b-multilang-8bit (lower cost tier for non-sensitive routing).

Early benchmark observations (attached snapshot):
- German/French intent classification: rw-multilang-7B-v2 at 94–96% accuracy on our seed prompts.
- Japanese/Hindi: 7B shows gaps on numeric tokenization (dates, amounts); 13B reduces missed numeric spans by ~18%.
- Noted regression risk: hallucination of masked account numbers when prompts include partial account tokens — we flagged this in the eval CSV.

Attachments included (stubs):
- prompt_sets_sample_v1.zip (sample prompts and expected labels, ~450 examples across languages)
- benchmarks_eu_apac_snapshot.csv (seed run, per-language metrics)

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Globex to share a 1k-2k anonymized sample of production utterances (priority languages). Target: 1 business day to collect.
2) Redwood to run focused suitability benchmarks on rw-multilang-7B-v2 & rw-instruct-13B with quantization profiles — deliver 1-week pilot report.
3) Security/procurement: I’ll send SOC2 and data-residency notes; Rahul please confirm preferred EU region (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
4) If pilot looks good, propose a 6-week pilot with an SLA-backed dedicated pool for peak-hours.

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm a sample delivery date for the 1k anonymized utterances?
- Any must-pass intents or extraction fields we should prioritize (e.g., IBAN, amount, currency)?

I’ll loop in engineering to size the perf runs. Thanks — quick call/demo after your sample upload works great.

— Hannah

Hannah — quick engineering readout below; attaching our small eval snapshot.

Short answers:
- Quantization profile: recommend Q3_4 for rw-multilang-7B-v2 (best balance of int8-like memory with lower FP degradation) for routing/intent classification. Use Q4_3 only if memory is the hard constraint and you accept ~3–5% drop on numeric-extraction F1.
- For rw-instruct-13B-multilingual, prefer 16-bit mixed (no quant) for the first pilot extraction tests — it materially reduces hallucination on numeric spans compared to 8-bit.

Estimated per-1k-token cost (ballpark, hosted):
- rw-multilang-7B-v2-quant (Q3_4): ~$0.60 per 1k tokens
- rw-instruct-13B-multilingual (16-bit): ~$2.10 per 1k tokens
\Performance (eu-central-1, x4 gpus reserved pool sim):
- 7B (Q3_4): p50 ~55ms, p95 ~210ms
- 13B (16-bit): p50 ~140ms, p95 ~520ms
\Suggested validation tests to include in pilot:
1) Numeric recall: injected partial-account tokens, measure false-positive inventions.
2) Locale tokenization: compare date/amount normalization across ja/hi vs de/fr.
3) Stress burst: 2x peak concurrency in a 30s window to confirm autoscaling.

I’ll queue a short bench on our eval cluster once Anna uploads the 1k sample (one run per model + quant profile). Please ask the customer to include a small holdout of edge-case examples (we see the most regressions there).

— Aditya
